newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Waterford Wedgwood silent on German deal.
newsitem.headline: Waterford Wedgwood silent on German deal.

text.p: Irish-based crystal and china firm Waterford Wedgwood said on Monday it would not comment on media speculation that it was planning to acquire loss-making German porcelain group Rosenthal.

A spokesman for Rosenthal earlier denied a German news magazine's weekend report that Waterford Wedgewood and Rosenthal had been in negotiations for several months and that the only obstacle to agreement was Rosenthal's five percent voting share limit.
Focus news magazine said the voting share clause prevented any company from owning more than five percent of Rosenthal's voting capital.
Rosenthal reported a loss of 10.7 million German marks in the first half of 1996 after a loss of 13.1 million marks in the year-earlier period.
The Focus magazine report said that Wedgwood hoped to increase its European presence by buying up Rosenthal.
